title: Channelized attention striping microkernel and KV soft-evict scheduler
author: Rina Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and unit cost for short-to-mid sequence inference workloads while keeping KV memory footprint under budget. This PR introduces a channelized attention microkernel that stripes Q/K/V across SIMD lanes/warps to improve L2 and shared-memory utilization for small batch, low-sequence scenarios, and a complementary KV soft-evict scheduler that probabilistically compacts and evicts cold KV entries to lower resident memory pressure during sustained continuous-batching.

Summary of changes: single continuous description string (no sections elsewhere) covering the kernel, scheduler, and rollout plan. The channelized microkernel reorganizes the inner-loop compute so that each warp processes interleaved channels of Q/K/V (instead of full-head blocks). This increases arithmetic intensity for narrow sequences and reduces bank conflicts seen on small sequence lengths. We add a small in-kernel rotary delta compaction step that applies a lightweight rematerialization-friendly encoding for rotary/rope components in the KV store (compact_rotary_storage) to reduce per-token KV bytes when rotary embeddings dominate. The soft-evict scheduler implements an occupancy- and recency-aware probabilistic eviction policy (soft_evict) with a tunable pressure parameter; it signals warmup/backpressure to the continuous-batcher to slow batching when memory thresholds approach configurable SLOs.

Why this is different: Unlike previous head/block tiling approaches, channelized striping is optimized for the common PLG short-seq patterns (seq_len <= 128, bursty arrivals) and purposely trades a small compute reordering latency for improved cache reuse and fewer warp replays under contention. The KV soft-evict is a non-blocking heuristic intended for Dedicated & Private deployments where memory isolation and predictable degradation are important; it intentionally avoids synchronous spilling to host storage and instead degrades gracefully while emitting observable metrics for automatic rerouting.

Checklist:
- [x] Microkernel: channelized striping compute + rotary delta compaction implemented in runtime/attn/channelized_kernel.cu
- [x] KV: compact rotary-backed storage and accessors in runtime/kv/compact_rotary_storage.cc/h
- [x] Scheduler: soft-evict implementation and config knobs in runtime/scheduler/soft_evict_scheduler.cpp
- [x] Continuous-batcher: backpressure hook and smoothing added to runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp
- [x] Benchmarks and unit tests added (tests/bench/attn_channelized_bench.py, tests/unit/kv_compact_test.cc)
- [x] Docs + rollout notes (docs/perf/attn_channelized.md)

Performance results (canary/LAB):
- Mixed short-seq synthetic workload (batch=1..8, seq=32..128): 8-12% p99 latency reduction vs. current main microkernel, 14-22% throughput improvement for mixed request distributions.
- End-to-end token cost reduced by ~7% in continuous-batcher steady-state when soft-evict reduces KV resident size by 18% on average for rotary-heavy models.

Backward compatibility & safety: Defaults are off for Hosted customers. Dedicated/Private deployments get the scheduler behind a runtime flag (runtime.config.attn_channelized.enabled = true) and can tune soft-evict thresholds. No API surface changes. There are additional metrics exposed (attn.channelized.enabled, kv.soft_evict_pressure, kv.rotary_compaction_ratio) and a canary rollout plan described in docs/perf/attn_channelized.md.

Rollout plan: Canary across 5 dedicated clusters with runtime flag enabled, monitor p99 latency, kv.resident_bytes, continuous_batcher.rate. If regressions >5% in token quality or >10% in p99 latency appear, automatic rollback.
commit_summary: 7 commits: initial channelized kernel prototype; rotary compaction data-structures; soft-evict scheduler; continuous-batcher backpressure hook; unit tests and bench; CI fixes for device-smoke; docs and rollout notes.
review_thread: Marcus Li (reviewer): Strong idea. Please annotate the kernel with expected lane occupancy and add a micro-benchmark that isolates L2 reuse. Also add a short paragraph describing numerical stability for rotary delta compaction.

Author (Rina): Added micro-bench and inline occupancy comments. Rotary compaction is reversible and uses int8 delta with bias accumulation to preserve fp16 fp32 accumulation paths; details in comments and tests.
Sofia Nguyen (reviewer): Concern: soft-evict may interact poorly with KMS-backed memory reporting in Private. Can we add a guard that disables evict when host-spill is configured?
Author (Rina): Added guard (runtime.config.kv_disable_soft_evict_when_spill=true by default false) and test coverage for the behavior. Also emitted a metric kv.soft_evict_disabled_reason for audit.
Diego Ramos (reviewer): CI flakes on cuda-smoke; requested smaller shared-memory footprint in the kernel.
ci_details: CI matrix: linux-x86 (unit) passed, linux-x86 (integration) passed, cuda-smoke initially failed (shared-mem too large) -> fixed in commit 4 -> full matrix green. Bench runner validated kernel correctness on Ampere and Hopper; Canary job ran on 5 clusters, results uploaded.
merge_outcome: Squash and merge on 2025-01-22 by Marcus Li. Release notes: Channelized attention microkernel (opt-in), KV soft-evict scheduler (configurable), compact rotary storage. Performance: 8-22% throughput/p99 improvements for short-seq workloads; opt-in for Hosted, rollout guidance for Dedicated/Private in docs/perf/attn_channelized.md.
